title: recipe-p2 — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of the p2 recipe's rich face, its first round at Sketch tier, remade once after its challenge: two made pieces that build the recipe exactly as it is written on its one voice and then test the note's own claims, one on the Method (the rule, the two pictures of 180°, the centre between 8 and 9, "no mirror axis", with a second voice offered as a repair) and one on the break and the clave (one break away from anything either recipe cooks, and where the section's break is exact), with the fingerprint of the words each was laid against and the offers the pieces measured for the text. The page is a bundle note with no frontmatter, so I am keyed by its file name, recipe-p2. I never hold the recipe's words.
grain: The page's own ## grain: five sections, two carry pieces. The opening (the H1's section) and What you should hear carry offers only.

offers.what: Step 2's rule, n → (n + 8) mod 16, is a slide, not a 180° turn on the strip. By definition it makes the half played twice. Measured: smallest repeat 8 steps or fewer in 126 of 126 halves, where the same meter reads 16 on recipe-pm's loop in 120 of 126. The 180° holds on the clock face: drawn round a circle, n → n + 8 is a half-turn, and on a loop a turn of the clock is a slide in time. On the strip, a half-turn about the point between 8 and 9 sends n to 17 − n, which is recipe-pm's map on one voice. The step's words, "mirror each hit's position and invert its placement", are ambiguous on one voice. On the note's own "8 steps doubled" they give 17 − n (pm); read as two reflections they give n + 8. Three honest fixes for Loudon: (a) add a second voice, the piece's proposed repair, where (n, voice) → (17 − n, other voice) is a half-turn that is not a mirror (1540 of 1568 voicings make the strip's p2); (b) stay on one voice, say that there p2's half-turn and pm's mirror coincide, and let the centre carry the difference; (c) keep the slide and name it: the clock's half-turn, a translation on the strip. If the slide is kept, write it n + 8, since on 1–16 the mod sends step 8 to 0.

offers.section: Recipe — Cooking p2 into a rhythmic phrase
offers.what: The opening says the pattern has "a center of rotational symmetry — but no mirror axis" (:3), and the Ingredients put that centre between 8 and 9 (:11). Measured on the loops the rule cooks: the centre between 8 and 9 holds in only 6 of 126, the halves that are their own reversal inside the eight. "No mirror axis" fails in 62 of 126 (the cooked tresillo has two). On one voice a half-turn centre is always a mirror axis, so the two claims can't both hold there; they can with a second voice (the Method offer's fix (a)).

A contradiction inside the text. :22 says p2 "echoes itself at a distance … What you played in the first half returns in the second half", and the rule does make the half again (by definition). :34 and recipe-pm.md:35 call p2 dialogue and pm echo. One possible fix, offered and not tested by ear: "What you played in the first half returns in the second, backwards and in the other voice", which needs the Method offer's second voice. The piece's repair step sets the half-turn beside the glide (the voices swapped, not reversed), so the reader can hear "another voice answers" apart from "it turns"; the agent heard neither.

"This is exactly where the clave lives" (and :24) is right about the break and wrong about where it starts. No loop this recipe cooks, broken once, becomes the son or rumba clave: 0 of 8960 tries each (126 halves × every one-step move of a second-half hit × 16 starting steps). recipe-pm's loops fail the same way, 0 of 7840. Both centres sit between two steps and pair every hit, so a cooked loop has an even number of hits, a break keeps the count, and a clave has five. The son clave (1 4 7 11 13) turns about one of its own steps: reversed through 4 and 12 it lands on itself, and on one voice that mirror is also a half-turn about step 4. On that group reading, :24's "not quite p2 … breaks the rotation slightly" holds. It fails only against the n + 8 rule. The nearest centre between steps splits 3 of the son clave's pairs. The section's break is exact once it starts from the clave: count it 2-3 (3 5 9 12 15), move 15 to 16, and it is the rumba clave (3 5 9 12 16). Proposed :24: "The Afro-Cuban clave is turned about one of its own steps, which this recipe's centre, between two steps, can never be; the rumba clave is that turn broken by one hit." :28 holds as written once the break starts from the son clave.

pieces.title: the recipe, cooked · six steps
pieces.caption: **The Method, done as written, on its one voice.** Write three or four hits in steps 1 to 8. The rule n → (n + 8) mod 16 makes the rest, and by definition that is the half played twice: the smallest repeat is 8 steps. pm's 17 − n sits beside it, its arcs nesting. The note's own "8 steps doubled" reads the Method's words that way too. Then 180° drawn two ways: turned on the clock, hits land at n + 8, the recipe; turned on the strip, at 17 − n, pm. A repair the note doesn't make, offered: a second voice, where the strip's half-turn is no longer a mirror, set beside the glide. The test, last, on the note's own claims: its centre between 8 and 9 holds in 6 of 126 cooked loops, and "no mirror axis" fails in 62. Checked in Node on the piece's own engine; the mix was not heard.

verdicts.why: Numbers all recompute (126, 120, 62, 1568, 1540), and step 4 (clock vs strip) is a real find; but step 5 says the note asks for a second voice, which it does not (one voice; its own 8-steps-doubled reading gives 17 − n = pm), and the test set before it cannot fail (n + 8 is the half twice by definition). Reword the second voice as one reading; test the note's own claims instead (centre at 8|9 holds in 6 of 126, no mirror axis fails in 62 of 126); label identities as identities; optionally add the glide map.

remade.what: Second voice reframed as a proposed repair, with a glide map beside it; the test moved to the note's own claims (centre at 8|9: 6/126; no mirror axis fails 62/126), identities labelled as identities.

pieces.title: the break and the clave · four steps
pieces.caption: **One break from the clave?** The tresillo, 1 4 7, cooked by the recipe into 1 4 7 9 12 15. Then one second-half hit moved one step, as the section says, and the son clave beside it on the clock. The test, its rule set first: no loop this recipe cooks reaches the son or rumba clave by one break (0 of 8960 each), and neither does recipe-pm (0 of 7840). Both centres sit between steps, so a cooked loop always has an even number of hits. The son clave turns about one of its own steps, 4 and 12: a mirror, and on one voice a half-turn. A centre between steps misses it by 3 pairs. And the section's break is exact from the clave: count it 2-3, move 15 to 16, and it is the rumba clave. Checked in Node on the piece's own engine; the mix was not heard.
pieces.near: This is exactly where the clave lives

verdicts.file: recipe-p2 — rich — the break and the clave.html
verdicts.why: 0 of 8960 and the parity argument confirmed, son clave exact through 4|12, rumba = son with 7 → 8; but 'the clave lives by pm, not here' overreaches: the arms compare a slide with a mirror, on one voice a half-turn about step 4 is that same mirror, and recipe-pm cooks the clave 0 of 7840 times too (its 8|9 centre pairs every hit). Rewrite the verdict around a centre through a step, add a between-steps mirror arm (son 3, rumba 1), and note the section's break is exact from son 2-3 (15 → 16).

remade.what: "Lives by pm" dropped; recipe-pm's reach (0/7840) and a between-steps arm (son 3, rumba 1) added; the section's break shown exact from the son clave 2-3 (15 → 16 = rumba).
